paper_title: NuSTAR bounds on radiatively decaying particles from M82
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, exactly as plotted on the y-axis of Fig. 2
notes: New observed astrophysical exclusion limit on axion-photon coupling from NuSTAR X-ray observations of the starburst galaxy M82, constraining heavy axions (30-500 keV) decaying a->gamma gamma. Not a dark matter search (no DM density assumption). The only explicit numerical limit value in the text is g_agamma = 0.75e-12 GeV^-1 at m_a = 316 keV (the 'central benchmark coupling' in Fig. 3 stated to correspond to the constraint obtained). Other data points are approximate reconstructions of the Fig. 2 exclusion contour based on the abstract's stated range (g ~ 1e-10 to 1e-12 GeV^-1 over 30-500 keV) and the statement that bounds are >1 order of magnitude stronger than prior astrophysical bounds in 30-300 keV; treat those points as approximate. Limit derived via TS=2.7 threshold (one-sided, 95% CL). | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.85, 36)) | Vision: Fig. 2 shows the novel NuSTAR M82 exclusion (thick red curve, region above excluded). X-axis: axion mass 10-800 keV (converted to eV); y-axis: axion-photon coupling g_agamma in GeV^-1, range ~3e-13 to 1e-10. Boundary starts at ~5e-12 GeV^-1 at 10 keV, reaches a broad minimum ~6e-13 GeV^-1 near 100-150 keV, then rises steeply above ~350 keV, hitting 1e-10 GeV^-1 near ~740 keV. Bound derived from axion production in M82 stars and decay a->2gamma (TS=2.7 threshold, ~90-95% CL; paper uses half-chi-squared with TS=2.7, i.e. 95% CL). Not a dark-matter search, so no DM density assumption.
